name: RI-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Gabe Amo running in a D+12 district
Overwhelming money edge: $1.85M on hand vs $2,332 for the Republican nominee
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at 99%
No public polls or expert ratings signal competition
model.rationale: The district's twelve-point Democratic lean, Amo's incumbency, and a roughly 800-to-1 cash-on-hand advantage leave the Republican challenger without visible resources, and prediction markets price a Democratic hold as near-certain. Nothing in the evidence justifies moving off a comfortable Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any surprise polling showing a single-digit race or unexpected outside spending against Amo would warrant a second look, but nothing currently signals a competitive contest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Rhode Island's First District, centered on Providence and nearby communities, leans about twelve points Democratic. Gabe Amo, first elected in a 2023 special election, is running for re-election and has built a large financial lead: $1.7 million raised and $1.85 million on hand. Republican Kellie Keenan has raised about $13,000 and reports just $2,300 in the bank, with an independent candidate also on the ballot but without reported fundraising.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on fundamentals. Prediction markets put the Democratic nominee's price near 99 cents, and the seat's partisanship, incumbency, and the lopsided money gap all point the same way. A Democratic hold is the strong expectation; the main uncertainty is the absence of field polling rather than any sign of a competitive race.
